raw_case_text:
A 50-year-old female presented with gradually progressive left-sided facial atrophy for the last 30 years. She also complained of intermittent left-sided headache for the last 8-9 years, which was throbbing, pulsatile with photophobia, phonophobia with history of visual auras. She had continuous tearing and redness of left eye since 3 years. There was no history of extraction of teeth, local trauma, seizures or lancinating pain suggestive of trigeminal neuralgia. The patient denied history of joint pains, rash, dyspnea, double vision and neurologic deficits in the extremities. Family history was non-contributory.
On examination, marked left-sided facial atrophy was present [Figure 1]. Oral cavity assessment disclosed left-sided tongue atrophy [Figure 2]. Ocular examination revealed enophthalmos and uveitis in left eye. The skin over left lower face had bluish hue. Rest of neurological examination was unremarkable. The investigations, including hematological parameters, blood sugar, serum creatinine, blood urea and liver function test revealed normal results. The C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate were not raised. The autoimmune markers, comprising antinuclear antibody, anti-double-stranded DNA antibody, anticardiolipin antibody and rheumatoid factor were non-reactive in sera. The viral studies for Epstein Barre virus, cytomegalovirus, dengue virus, herpes simplex virus and Japanese encephalitis virus showed negative results. Electroencephalography was reported to be normal. Magnetic resonance imaging of cranium did not demonstrate any abnormality [Figure 3]. Facial nerve stimulation at anterior ear on both sides revealed minor differences in latency and amplitudes [Figure 4]. Blink reflex on stimulation of supraorbital nerves showed insignificant differences of R2-R1, on left side 27.95 ms, while on right side 24.20 ms [Figure 5]. The clinical description and laboratory evaluation suggested the diagnosis of facial atrophy of Romberg and migraine with aura. The patient was prescribed propranolol 40 mg twice a day, flunarizine 10 mg/day as prophylactics for migraine along with abortive medications for control of acute headache. The patient was not willing for facial reconstructive surgery. On follow up after 6 months, her frequency of headache was significantly decreased.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 50-year-old female presented with a 30-year history of progressive left-sided facial atrophy, an 8-9 year history of intermittent throbbing left-sided headaches with visual aura, and a 3-year history of left eye tearing and redness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced insidiously progressive left hemifacial wasting over 30 years, accompanied for the past 8-9 years by pulsatile left-sided headaches with photophobia, phonophobia, and visual auras, and for the past 3 years by continuous epiphora and redness of the left eye.
subjective.past_medical_history: No history of dental extraction, local facial trauma, or seizures; non-contributory family history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for progressive left facial atrophy, throbbing left hemicranial headache, photophobia, phonophobia, visual auras, and left ocular tearing and redness. Negative for lancinating trigeminal neuralgia pain, arthralgia, rash, dyspnea, diplopia, or extremity neurological deficits.

objective.physical_examination: Marked left-sided facial atrophy with a bluish cutaneous hue over the left lower face, left-sided tongue hemiatrophy on oral exam, and left-sided enophthalmos and uveitis on ocular examination; remainder of the neurological examination was normal.
objective.routine_investigations: CBC, blood glucose, serum creatinine, blood urea, liver function tests, CRP, and ESR were all normal. Autoimmune panel (ANA, anti-dsDNA, anticardiolipin antibody, and rheumatoid factor) and viral serologies for EBV, CMV, HSV, and Japanese encephalitis virus were non-reactive. EEG was normal; facial nerve stimulation and supraorbital blink reflex testing showed only minor/insignificant side-to-side latency differences (R2-R1 27.95 ms left vs. 24.20 ms right).
objective.advanced_workup: Cranial MRI demonstrated no intracranial parenchymal or vascular abnormality.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Parry-Romberg syndrome (progressive hemifacial atrophy) associated with migraine with aura and left uveitis. Dengue virus infection was ruled out by negative viral serology, along with EBV, CMV, HSV, JEV, and systemic autoimmune disease. Treated with oral propranolol 40 mg twice daily, flunarizine 10 mg daily, and abortive migraine medications (patient declined facial reconstructive surgery), resulting in a significant reduction in headache frequency at 6-month follow-up.
